findings.reason: it decides where the change lives, and implemented at the stated locus alone the pass records a spurious failure and backs the request off, the opposite of the deliverable's "leaves that request queued ... and records no failure"; naming the pass (or `admission_launch`) as the caller that leaves the request untouched is what makes the stated outcome reach a done-when that only asserts the pointer's survival.
findings.text: §18 places the queue-behind decision in the scope check ("the scope check neither refuses on it nor drops it, and instead turns an overlap with it into 'queue behind'") and does not name the admission pass as detecting the overlap before it releases the pointer; if the pass only learns of the overlap when `dispatch` returns a queued record, `_require_launched_record` raises (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:521, "dispatch did not return a launched record") and `_record_queued_failure` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:485) stamps the pointer with a failure and a bounded `retry_at`, which contradicts "records no failure" and starts a back-off for a request that is merely waiting its turn
